before.title: Symmetric hyperbolic reduction of the Einstein-scalar system and on-shell conservation
before.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and
let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model with scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor
$T_{ab}=K[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}(\tfrac12\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi))]$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]). Fix a chart and the background
$\bar g,\bar\nabla$ of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then
the system consisting of the reduced Einstein equation with this $T$ and the
scalar equation, together with the definition of the auxiliary variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\bar\nabla_ig_{ab},\ \varphi,\ \varphi_0:=\bar\nabla_0\varphi,\ \varphi_i:=\bar\nabla_i\varphi\bigr)$$
is, on every region where the metric is Lorentzian and the chart is initially
orthogonal, a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system whose time
matrix is block diagonal with positive definite blocks: the metric block
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) and, for the scalar
variables, a positive definite block built from $1$ and $-g^{00}$; the coupling
between the metric and scalar blocks is only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of $g$. Moreover the stress-energy tensor is on-shell
divergence-free: $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ whenever $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$
([[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]).

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.4 (Matter Models): the conditions defining a matter model and the treatment of scalar-field matter coupled to the Einstein equations

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 3.1 (Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems): the definition of a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system, the finite-dimensional mollifier approximation (3.1) solved by ODE theory, the energy and Moser product/composition estimates, the higher-order energy inequality, uniqueness, the Rellich/Ascoli compactness step and the passage to a classical solution, with Remarks 1-6 on smooth persistence, the continuation criterion, Cauchy stability and the non-identity time matrix

statement.after:
Fix one scalar model with smooth potential $V$ and fixed stress normalization $K_\phi$ as in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]. On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold its equations and stress are
$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad T_{ab}=K_\phi\left[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\left(\tfrac12g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\partial_d\varphi+V(\varphi)\right)\right].$$
Fix a chart and a smooth background $\bar g$ for the reduced Einstein equation of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. On the open state set where $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the reduced Einstein equation coupled to this scalar equation has a smooth first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction with variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},\varphi,P=\partial_0\varphi,Q_i=\partial_i\varphi).$$
The time matrix is block diagonal with metric block $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ and scalar block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. Matter and metric cross-coupling is zeroth order in derivatives of $z$. The partial-derivative metric variables and the background-covariant ones are related by an invertible smooth zeroth-order change of variables; either gives the reduction.

For complete initial scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ in an initially orthogonal chart with $\partial_0=n$, prescribe $(\varphi,P,Q_i)=(\varphi_0,\pi_0,\partial_i\varphi_0)$. The auxiliary constraints propagate, the reconstructed scalar solves its full equation on the reduced metric, and its stress is conserved there before imposing the unreduced Einstein equation. Conversely every smooth physical scalar solution extracts to the same system. No potential positivity or mass sign is required; local arguments do not require a global orientation.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$, $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=0$. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u,\bar\nabla u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that it is divergence-free
exactly on the solutions of the scalar equation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither statement, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently $T$ is divergence-free, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, exactly on the
solutions of the scalar equation of motion.

derivations.claim:
(Scalar block.) Introduce $(\varphi,\varphi_0,\varphi_i)$ with the relations $ ar
abla_0\varphi=\varphi_0$, $ ar
abla_0\varphi_i= ar
abla_i\varphi_0$. By [L1] the scalar equation is equivalent to $ ar
abla_0\varphi_0=-(g^{00})^{-1}[2g^{0i} ar
abla_i\varphi_0+g^{ij} ar
abla_i\varphi_j+	ext{lower-order}]$, i.e., a first-order system with time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$ on the slots $(\varphi,\varphi_0,\varphi_i)$: symmetric and positive definite exactly when $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})>0$.

(Coupling and total symbol.) The metric equation of [L2] contains the matter stress tensor $T$; by [L3] $T$ is a smooth function of $(g,\varphi)$ and the first derivatives $\varphi_0,\varphi_i$ only, so its contribution to the first-order system for $u$ is a zeroth-order (in derivatives of $u$) source, and it couples to the metric block only through $g$ itself. The combined time matrix is block diagonal with the two positive blocks of steps 1.1 and [L2], hence positive definite; the spatial coefficient matrices are symmetric because each block is and the coupling carries no spatial derivatives mixing the blocks.

(Conservation.) On-shell conservation of $T$ is [L4]; hence the matter sector satisfies the hypothesis of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]. [L4] ∎

$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1},\bar g$
and the background curvature. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$, $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=0$. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(u,\bar\nabla u;\bar g)\Bigr],$$
and the resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

smooth symmetric $2$-tensor

with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that it is divergence-free
exactly on the solutions of the scalar equation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither statement, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently $T$ is divergence-free, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, exactly on the
solutions of the scalar equation of motion.

on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields

**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of

nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b=\delta^c{}_bg^{ab}(q),$$
